extracted.intended_audience: users of polymake / SINGULAR libraries (computational geometers, algebraic geometers, and developers using polymake.lib)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for polymake.lib procedures operating on polytopes, cones, fans, and related lattice/combinatorial invariants. Each entry lists usage, assumptions, return type, notes, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: facetWidths
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: facetWidths(p); p polytope
Assume: isBounded(p)==1
Return: intvec, vector with the integral widths of all facet normals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure from library polymake.lib. Example demonstrates creating a polytope via points and calling facetWidths; output is an intvec (e.g. 1,2,1,2).

rubrics_metrics.name: gorensteinIndex
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: gorensteinIndex(p); p polytope
Assume: isGorenstein(p)==1
Return: int, a factor n such that n*p+v is reflexive for some translation v
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the translation v can be computed via gorensteinVector(p). Example shows output 2 for a sample polytope.

rubrics_metrics.name: gorensteinVector
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: gorensteinVector(p); p polytope
Assume: isGorenstein(p)==1
Return: intvec, a vector v such that n*p+v is reflexive for some factor n
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the factor n can be computed via gorensteinIndex(p). Example shows output intvec (e.g. 1,1,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: hStarVector
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: hStarVector(p); p polytope
Return: intvec, the h* vector of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example includes warnings from external tools (LattE) when parsing fails. Output example: 1,3,11,1. Procedure may call external packages (libnormaliz, latte) and emit warnings if parsing fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: hVector
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: hVector(p); p polytope
Return: intvec, the h vector of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example calls hVector on a sample polytope; polymake may use external packages (lrs, ppl). Example output: 1,3,3,1.

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbertBasis
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: hilbertBasis(c); c cone
Return: intmat, the Hilbert basis of c intersected with Z^n
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows invocation on a cone via points; polymake may use package 4ti2. Example output lists the Hilbert basis rows.

rubrics_metrics.name: interiorLatticePoints
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: interiorLatticePoints(p); p polytope
Assume: isBounded(p)==1
Return: intmat, all lattice points in the relative interior of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates output (e.g. 1,0,0 or 1,1,1). polymake may call external tools (ppl) and show related messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: isBounded
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isBounded(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if p is bounded; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows calling isBounded on two polytopes, one bounded (returns 1) and one unbounded (returns 0).

rubrics_metrics.name: isCanonical
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isCanonical(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if p has exactly one interior lattice point; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example may show external tool warnings (LattE) when computing interior lattice points. Example returns 1 for a sample polytope; isReflexive can be queried afterwards.

rubrics_metrics.name: isCompressed
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isCompressed(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if p has maximal facet width 1; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows two polytopes: one with output 0 and another with output 1. polymake may use PPL and other packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: isGorenstein
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isGorenstein(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if p is Gorenstein, i.e. reflexive modulo dilatation and translation; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates output 1 for a Gorenstein polytope and 0 for a non-Gorenstein one.

rubrics_metrics.name: isLatticeEmpty
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isLatticeEmpty(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if p contains no lattice points other than the vertices; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show output 1 and 0 for different polytopes; external tool warnings (LattE) may appear when counting lattice points.

rubrics_metrics.name: isNormal
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isNormal(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if the projective toric variety defined by p is projectively normal; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows polymake using 4ti2 and PPL; example returns 0 for the sample polytope.

rubrics_metrics.name: isReflexive
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isReflexive(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if p is reflexive; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows usage on two polytopes returning 1 in examples; polymake may report use of PPL.

rubrics_metrics.name: isSmooth
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isSmooth(c); c cone
       isSmooth(f); f fan
       isSmooth(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if the input is smooth; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include cones, fans, and polytopes. Demonstrates combining cones into fans and checking smoothness; outputs vary (1 or 0). polymake may use PPL and report results for cones, fans, polytopes (e.g. some polytopes are not smooth).

rubrics_metrics.name: isTerminal
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isTerminal(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if p has exactly one interior lattice point and all other lattice points are vertices; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show outputs 1 and 0 for different polytopes; external LattE warnings may appear. Relationship to isCanonical/isReflexive is demonstrated in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: isVeryAmple
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: isVeryAmple(p); p polytope
Return: 1, if p is very ample; 0 otherwise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show calls on sample polytopes returning 1. polymake may use PPL and 4ti2 internally.

rubrics_metrics.name: latticeCodegree
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: latticeCodegree(p); p polytope
Return: int, the smallest number n such that n*p has a relative interior lattice point
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: dimension(p)+1==latticeDegree(p)+latticeCodegree(p). Examples show outputs like 2 and 4 for sample polytopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: latticeDegree
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: latticeDegree(p); p polytope
Return: int, the degree of the Ehrhart polynomial of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: dimension(p)+1==latticeDegree(p)+latticeCodegree(p). Examples show outputs like 1 and 0. polymake may call external tools (PPL).

rubrics_metrics.name: latticePoints
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: latticePoints(p); p polytope
Assume: isBounded(p)==1
Return: intmat, all lattice points in p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show listing of all integer lattice points in the polytope. polymake may use PPL and other packages; outputs are intmat lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: latticeVolume
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: latticeVolume(p); p polytope
Assume: isBounded(p)==1
Return: int, the lattice volume of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show latticeVolume outputs (e.g. 2, 3, 1) for sample polytopes. polymake reports used packages (PPL) in output.

rubrics_metrics.name: maximalFace
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: maximalFace(p,v); p polytope, v intvec
Assume: v lies in the negative dual tail cone of p
Return: intmat, vertices of the face of p on which the linear form v is maximal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the maximal face is independent of the first coordinate of v since p is considered as a polytope in the plane (first coordinate)=1. Examples show calling with different v and receiving vertex lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: maximalValue
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: maximalValue(p,v); p polytope, v intvec
Assume: v lies in the negative dual tail cone of p
Return: intmat, vertices of the face of p on which the linear form v is maximal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: first coordinate of v corresponds to a shift of the maximal value since p is considered as a polytope in the plane (first coordinate)=1. Examples show numeric maximal values (e.g. 1, -4).

rubrics_metrics.name: minimalFace
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: minimalFace(p,v); p polytope, v intvec
Assume: v lies in the dual tail cone of p
Return: intmat, vertices of the face of p on which the linear form v is minimal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the minimal face is independent of the first coordinate of v since p is considered as a polytope in the plane (first coordinate)=1. Examples show vertex lists for minimal faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: minimalValue
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: minimalValue(p,v); p polytope, v intvec
Assume: v lies in the negative dual tail cone of p
Return: intmat, vertices of the face of p on which the linear form v is minimal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: first coordinate of v corresponds to a shift of the minimal value since p is considered as a polytope in the plane (first coordinate)=1. Examples show numeric minimal values (e.g. -1, 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: minkowskiSum
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: minkowskiSum(c,d); c cone, d cone
       minkowskiSum(c,q); c cone, q polytope
       minkowskiSum(p,d); p polytope, d cone
       minkowskiSum(p,q); p polytope, q polytope
Assume: input arguments have the same ambient dimension
Return: cone, if both inputs are cones; polytope, otherwise — the minkowski sum of the two input arguments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show usage on polytopes p and q and retrieving vertices(minkowskiSum(p,q)). Output is the summed polytope; polymake reports used packages such as PPL.

rubrics_metrics.name: nBoundaryLatticePoints
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: nBoundaryLatticePoints(p); p polytope
Assume: isBounded(p)==1
Return: int, the number of lattice points in the relative boundary of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show outputs like 9 and 2 for sample polytopes. External tool warnings (LattE) may appear when computing lattice counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: nHilbertBasis
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: nHilbertBasis(c); c cone
Return: int, the number of elements in the Hilbert basis of c intersected with Z^n
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates polymake using 4ti2 and returns an integer (e.g. 10).

rubrics_metrics.name: nInteriorLatticePoints
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: nInteriorLatticePoints(p); p polytope
Assume: isBounded(p)==1
Return: int, the number of lattice points in the relative interior of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show output (e.g. 1). External tool warnings (LattE) may be displayed during computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: nLatticePoints
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: nLatticePoints(p); p polytope
Assume: isBounded(p)==1
Return: intmat, the number of lattice points in p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show outputs like 10 and 3 for sample polytopes. LattE-related warnings may appear in output.

rubrics_metrics.name: normalFan
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: normalFan(p); p polytope
Return: fan, the normal fan of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example prints a PolyhedralFan application output including AMBIENT_DIM, DIM, RAYS, N_RAYS, F_VECTOR, SIMPLICIAL, PURE, CONES, MAXIMAL_CONES, etc. polymake reports used packages (PPL).

rubrics_metrics.name: vertexAdjacencyGraph
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: vertexAdjacencyGraph(p); p polytope
Return: list, the first entry is a bigintmat containing all vertices as row vectors; the second entry is a list of intvecs representing the adjacency graph of the vertices of p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows the returned [1] vertex matrix and [2] adjacency lists where entry i contains all vertices j connected to vertex i via an edge. Output formatting in examples may include empty placeholders and integer lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: vertexEdgeGraph
rubrics_metrics.description:
Usage: vertexEdgeGraph(p); p polytope
Return: list, the first entry is a bigintmat containing all vertices as row vectors; the second entry is a list of intvecs representing the edge graph of the vertices of p (each intvec represents an edge connecting vertex i with vertex j)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows returned vertex matrix and edge pairs (e.g. 0,5; 1,2; etc.). polymake prints the matrix and edge list entries in its output.
